Which coding agents can use ticketd?

Any agent or harness that can run shell commands and read their output. There’s no plugin or MCP server to install: your agent calls the ticketd CLI, which prints JSON. Describe the commands in its instructions, for example in AGENTS.md.

Where are my tickets stored?

In a local workspace: a SQLite database in your user’s application-data folder, outside your repositories. The desktop app and the CLI open it directly, with no account, server or background service. Uninstalling keeps it, and ticketd backup saves a copy.

What do I need to install?

The desktop app and the ticketd CLI. Each download has both, for macOS 26 on Apple Silicon, Ubuntu 24.04 (x86-64) or Windows 11 (x86-64). Put the CLI on the PATH your agent uses. Downloads are unsigned build artifacts for now, so your system may warn before opening them; the install guide walks through it.

How is it different from my agent’s own to-do list?

An agent’s built-in plan or to-do list usually lives in its session. ticketd keeps tickets, Documents and updates in a local workspace that you can open in the app and any later session can read. It doesn’t run agents, assign work or orchestrate them.
